recipes.title: Conch Fritters: Bahamian Style
recipes.description: A traditional Bahamian recipe made with conch, the wonderful shellfish. These fritters are great as appetizers, finger foods or very tasty hors d'oeuvres. Conch can be replaced with calamari, shrimp, imitation crab meat and lobster. BEWARE - these are HOT!

ingredients.prep_note: or Pickapeppa Sauce, for dipping sauce

instructions.text: Heat the oil in large pot or deep fryer to 365°F (185 degrees C).
In a bowl, mix the flour, egg and milk.
Season with cayenne pepper, seasoning salt, salt, pepper and red pepper flakes.
Mix in the conch meat, onion, red & yellow & green bell pepper, celery and garlic.
Drop the batter by rounded tablespoons into the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
BE CAREFUL!
Remove the basket or with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Now, is the time to slightly season, again.
In a bowl, mix the ketchup, "lime" juice, mayonnaise, hot sauce, salt & pepper.
Serve dipping sauce on the side with the fritters.
Enjoy!

notes: Can substitute conch with calamari, shrimp, imitation crab meat, or lobster

recipes.title: Picante Dip
recipes.description: Creamy tomato and onion dip with cream cheese, served with tostadas.

instructions.text: Simmer the tomatoes and onions about 20 minutes. Cool and stir until it is only warm.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix to the desired consistency for a dip.
Serve with tostadas.

recipes.title: Green Chile Dip
recipes.description: Simple sour cream dip with green chiles and garlic, served with tortilla or potato chips.

instructions.text: Mix all the ingredients.
Serve with tortilla chips or potato chips.

recipes.title: Avocado Dip
recipes.description: Guacamole-style dip with Colby cheese, green chiles, and green onions.

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and chill.

recipes.title: Chile-izzas
recipes.description: Mini pizza bites with ground beef, biscuits, tomato sauce, cheese, and green chiles.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Brown the ground beef and drain. Salt to taste.
Separate the biscuits and roll them out into circles. Place them on a greased cookie sheet and spread tomato sauce on them.
Add a layer of meat, then chilies top with cheese. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cut each circle into quarters and serve hot.

notes: Variation: Add sour cream or substitute pork sausage for the ground beef

recipes.title: Perritos Verdes (Green Chile Puppies)
recipes.description: Hot dogs wrapped with green chile strips and tortillas, deep fried until crispy.

instructions.text: Wrap the franks in strips of green chile or slice them partially through and fill the openings with green chile sauce.
Wrap tortilla strips around the franks and secure them with toothpicks.
Fry them briefly in hot deep fat until crisp.

recipes.title: Chile-Cheese Squares
recipes.description: A cheesy appetizer with layers of cheddar and green chiles topped with eggs.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer the cheese and chiles in a buttered baking dish.
Pour the eggs over and dust with the paprika.
Bake for 30 minutes or until it tests done.
Cut into small squares and serve as an appetizer.

notes: Variation: Use ½ lb cheddar and ½ lb Monterey Jack cheese. Garnish with black olives and pimento.
Variation: Use whole green chiles to line a pie pan. Spread ½ lb grated cheddar over the chiles. Beat 8 eggs with 2 tbsp cream and salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.title: Chil-E-Ums
recipes.description: Bite-sized rolls filled with bacon, onion, and green chiles.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Prepare the hot roll mix following the directions on the box.
Break up the bacon, chop the onion, and mix together with the green chiles.
Divide the roll mix into 48 equal parts.
Using your hands, spread out each piece and fill with ½ to ¾ teaspoon of the filling mixture.
Pinch the rolls together and bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Chile-Izzos
recipes.description: Biscuit rounds topped with beef and cheese, baked until done.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brown the ground beef and drain. Salt to taste.
Separate the biscuits and roll them out into circles. Place them on a greased cookie sheet and spread tomato sauce on them.
Add a layer of meat, then chile, then top with cheese.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Cut each circle into quarters and serve hot.

notes: Variation: Add sour cream or substitute pork sausage for the ground beef.

recipes.title: Perritos Verdes (Green Chile Puppies)
recipes.description: Hot dogs wrapped in green chile strips and tortillas, then deep-fried.

ingredients.prep_note: cooked, or 1 lb cut into 1.5-inch strips

instructions.text: Wrap the franks in strips of green chile or slice them partially through and fill the openings with green chile sauce.
Wrap tortilla strips around the franks and secure them with toothpicks.
Fry them briefly in hot deep fat until crisp.

recipes.title: Chile-Mushroom Fritters
recipes.description: Crispy fried fritters with mushrooms and green chiles.

instructions.text: In mixing bowl, combine biscuit mix, mushrooms, onion, chile, salt and celery seed.
Mix together egg yolk and sour cream; stir into dry ingredients just until moistened.
Beat egg white to stiff peaks. Gently fold beaten egg white into mushroom mixture.
In heavy saucepan or electric deep-fat fryer, heat oil to 375 degrees.
Drop batter by tablespoonfuls into hot oil. Fry about 2 minutes or until golden brown, turning once. Transfer to rack to drain.

recipes.title: Pecorino with Honey and Walnuts
recipes.description: A simple Italian appetizer pairing sharp Pecorino with sweet honey and crunchy walnuts.

instructions.text: Arrange Pecorino wedges on a serving board.
Scatter toasted walnuts around the cheese.
Drizzle honey generously over the cheese.
Add pear slices if using.
Serve with crusty bread or crackers.

notes: Use aged Pecorino Toscano for a milder flavor or Pecorino Romano for sharper taste
Pairs beautifully with a robust red wine

recipes.title: Manchego with Membrillo (Quince Paste)
recipes.description: The classic Spanish pairing of nutty Manchego cheese with sweet quince paste. Simple perfection.

instructions.text: Arrange Manchego slices on a serving board.
Place membrillo slices alongside the cheese.
Scatter Marcona almonds around the board.
Serve with crusty bread. Instruct guests to pair a piece of cheese with membrillo in each bite.

notes: True Manchego is made only from Manchega sheep milk in La Mancha, Spain
Look for Denominación de Origen label for authentic Manchego

recipes.title: Manchego Croquetas
recipes.description: Crispy fried croquettes filled with creamy béchamel and Manchego cheese. A beloved Spanish bar snack.

instructions.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in warm milk. Cook, stirring constantly, until very thick, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Manchego, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until cheese melts.
Spread mixture in a baking dish. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Shape cold mixture into small cylinders or ovals using wet hands.
Dip each croqueta in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Double-coat for extra crunch.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry croquetas in batches until golden, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

notes: Can add jamón serrano to the béchamel
Croquetas can be frozen before frying

recipes.title: Endive Boats with Roquefort and Pear
recipes.description: Crisp endive leaves filled with Roquefort, pear, and walnuts. An elegant appetizer.

instructions.text: Blend Roquefort and cream cheese until smooth.
Fold in half the diced pear and half the walnuts.
Spoon or pipe mixture into endive leaves.
Top each with remaining pear, walnuts, and a drizzle of honey.
Garnish with snipped chives.
Arrange on platter and serve immediately.

notes: Can substitute radicchio cups if endive unavailable
Prepare filling ahead, assemble just before serving

recipes.title: Classic Swiss Cheese Fondue
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss fondue with Gruyère and Emmental, white wine, and kirsch. Perfect for sharing.

instructions.text: Rub fondue pot with cut garlic. Discard garlic.
Add wine and lemon juice. Heat over medium until simmering.
Toss cheeses with cornstarch.
Add cheese by handfuls, stirring constantly in a figure-8 motion.
Wait for each addition to melt before adding more.
Once smooth, stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper.
Transfer to fondue pot over low flame.
Serve with bread cubes for dipping. Stir occasionally.

notes: If fondue gets too thick, add a splash of warm wine
Also great with apple slices, vegetables, or small potatoes

recipes.title: Baked Brie with Honey and Nuts
recipes.description: Warm, gooey brie topped with honey, walnuts, and fresh rosemary. An irresistible appetizer.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place brie on a small baking dish or oven-safe plate.
Score the top rind in a crosshatch pattern (optional - helps cheese ooze).
Bake 12-15 minutes until soft and gooey inside.
Drizzle with honey and top with nuts and rosemary.
Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Serve immediately with crackers or bread.

notes: Don't overbake or cheese will run everywhere
Can add fig jam or dried cranberries

recipes.title: Brie en Croûte
recipes.description: Brie wrapped in golden puff pastry with a layer of jam. Impressive yet easy.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line baking sheet with parchment.
Roll puff pastry slightly larger if needed.
Spread jam on top of brie.
Place brie jam-side down in center of pastry.
Fold pastry up and over brie, pleating to enclose. Trim excess.
Flip seam-side down onto baking sheet.
Brush with egg wash. Score decorative pattern if desired.
Bake 20-25 minutes until pastry is deep golden.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Letting it rest prevents cheese from running out when cut
Can add prosciutto or dried fruit inside

recipes.title: Labneh Dip with Za'atar and Olive Oil
recipes.description: Creamy strained yogurt cheese drizzled with olive oil and za'atar. Essential Middle Eastern mezze.

instructions.text: Spread labneh on a plate or shallow bowl, creating a well in the center.
Pool olive oil in the well.
Sprinkle generously with za'atar.
Add mint and pine nuts if using.
Finish with Aleppo pepper.
Serve with warm pita for scooping.

notes: Za'atar is a blend of thyme, sumac, and sesame - essential for this dish
Can shape labneh into balls and roll in za'atar for a different presentation

recipes.title: Classic Provoleta Argentina
recipes.source_note: Traditional Argentine grilled cheese, created by Italian immigrants in 1940s Buenos Aires
recipes.description: Grilled provolone cheese with oregano and red pepper flakes, the essential opening act of an Argentine asado.

instructions.text: Let cheese come to room temperature for 30 minutes to an hour before cooking. This helps form a better crust.
Lightly coat a cast iron skillet with olive oil and place over medium-high heat (375-400°F) on grill or stovetop.
When skillet is hot, place the cheese wheel in the pan.
Sprinkle oregano and red pepper flakes over the top of the cheese.
Cover and cook for about 5 minutes until cheese is fully melted, bubbly, and edges are golden brown and crispy.
Carefully remove from heat and serve immediately with toasted bread for dipping.

notes: Use a cast iron skillet to prevent cheese from melting through grill grates
Best enjoyed immediately while hot and gooey
For indoor cooking, finish under broiler for golden crust

recipes.title: Provoleta with Chimichurri
recipes.source_note: Provoleta served with traditional chimichurri sauce
recipes.description: Grilled provolone topped with fresh, herbaceous chimichurri sauce for a burst of Argentine flavor.

instructions.text: Make chimichurri: Combine parsley, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, and both vinegars in a mortar and pestle or food processor. Work into a thick paste.
Add salt and olive oil, mixing until you have a thick, chunky sauce. Set aside.
Set up grill for two-zone cooking with one side at high heat.
Preheat a cast iron skillet over high heat, then move to indirect heat zone.
Place cold cheese directly over high heat for 2 minutes to brown the bottom.
Transfer cheese to the hot skillet and cover until melted and bubbly, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, brush baguette slices with oil and grill until charred, about 1 minute per side.
Top hot melted cheese with a generous dollop of chimichurri and serve with grilled bread.

notes: Chimichurri can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 1 week
Hand-chopping herbs gives better texture than food processor
Chimichurri should be loose and chunky, not paste-like

recipes.title: Provoleta with Salsa Criolla
recipes.attribution: Argentine grilled cheese with fresh vegetable relish
recipes.source_note: Provoleta served with traditional salsa criolla
recipes.description: Grilled provolone served with salsa criolla, a zesty relish of fresh tomatoes, peppers, and onions.

instructions.text: Make salsa criolla: Combine olive oil, vinegar, parsley, garlic, bell pepper, onion, and tomato in a medium bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 425°F with rack in upper third.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add provolone and sprinkle half the oregano and pepper flakes on top.
Cook, flipping once, until cheese bubbles and edges brown, 4-6 minutes total.
Transfer to oven and bake until melted and golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Top with remaining oregano and pepper flakes.
Serve immediately with salsa criolla and sliced baguette.

notes: Salsa criolla can be made up to 4 hours ahead
The relish should be fresh and crunchy, not cooked
Let cheese come to room temperature before cooking for best crust

recipes.title: Sardo Cheese Crostini with Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.source_note: Toasted bread topped with Argentine grating cheese and sun-dried tomatoes
recipes.description: Crispy crostini topped with sharp Sardo cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, and fresh herbs.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange baguette slices on a baking sheet. Brush lightly with olive oil.
Bake until golden and crisp, 5-6 minutes.
While still warm, rub each slice with the cut side of garlic clove.
Top each crostini with sun-dried tomato slices.
Sprinkle generously with grated Sardo cheese.
Return to oven for 2 minutes until cheese is slightly melted.
Top with fresh basil leaf and crack of black pepper. Serve warm.

notes: Sardo's sharp, salty flavor pairs perfectly with sweet sun-dried tomatoes
Can substitute fresh tomatoes in summer
Add a drizzle of balsamic reduction for extra flavor

recipes.title: Picada Argentina with Magnasco Edam
recipes.source_note: Argentine snack board featuring the country's distinctive Edam cheese
recipes.description: A traditional Argentine snack platter featuring Magnasco Edam alongside cured meats, olives, and accompaniments.

instructions.text: Select a large wooden board or platter for presentation.
Arrange cubed or sliced Magnasco Edam cheese in the center of the board.
Fan salami and ham slices on one side of the cheese.
Place olives in small bowls or pile directly on the board.
Scatter nuts around the board.
Add bread slices and breadsticks along the edges.
Place small dishes of mayonnaise and mustard for dipping.
If using quince paste, cut into small squares and arrange near the cheese.
Serve with red wine at room temperature for the traditional experience.

notes: Picada comes from the verb 'picar' meaning to pick at or nibble
Magnasco Edam is dryer and harder than Dutch Edam, perfect for slicing
This is Argentina's answer to charcuterie boards, enjoyed before asado or with evening wine

recipes.title: Magnasco Edam with Wine and Crackers
recipes.source_note: Simple presentation of Argentina's distinctive Edam cheese
recipes.description: Argentine Magnasco Edam served simply with crackers and paired with robust red wine.

instructions.text: Remove Magnasco Edam from refrigerator 30 minutes before serving to bring to room temperature.
Cut a wedge from the Edam ball to reveal the interior. Alternatively, cut into cubes or thin slices.
Arrange crackers in a fan pattern on a serving board.
Place cheese wedge or cubes in the center.
Add grapes, dried apricots, and walnuts around the cheese.
Open red wine and let it breathe for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve cheese at room temperature with wine.

notes: Magnasco is Argentina's oldest dairy, founded by Italian immigrants 155 years ago
Argentine Edam is sharper and harder than Dutch Edam
The red wax coating is traditional and beautiful for presentation
Pairs excellently with Argentine Malbec

missing_inputs: 1 bottle Malbec or robust red wine

recipes.title: Divine Baked Feta
recipes.description: Simple baked feta with olive oil, crushed red pepper, and oregano. Surprisingly mild despite the heat.

ingredients.item: bread rounds or crackers for serving

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 300°F.
Slice feta and arrange in an oven-safe dish.
Drizzle generously with olive oil.
Sprinkle heavily with crushed red pepper (seeds and all).
Add crushed oregano (dried is fine, but not powdered).
Grind fresh black pepper over the top.
Bake for 10 minutes until feta is soft and warm.
Serve immediately with bread rounds or crackers.

notes: Feta's saltiness balances the pepper heat
Use crushed dried oregano, not powdered
Serve immediately while warm and soft

recipes.title: Israeli-Style Hummus
recipes.description: Authentic smooth hummus made from scratch with dried chickpeas. Served warm with olive oil.

instructions.text: Soak chickpeas overnight in cold water with 1 tbsp baking soda (speeds cooking).
Drain and rinse well. Place in pressure cooker covered by 2 inches water.
Bring to boil, skim foam, then cook 1-1.5 hours until beans are 'soft as butter'.
CRITICAL: Never add salt during cooking - beans won't soften.
Separate cooked beans from liquid, reserving both.
Pass beans through sieve to remove skins for smoothest texture.
While still warm: add half the lemon juice, 3-4 tbsp hot cooking water, minced garlic, tahini, and salt.
Mix thoroughly. Taste and adjust lemon, salt, and consistency.
Serve warm in bowls topped with whole chickpeas, cooking liquid, generous olive oil, and paprika.
Serve with fresh pita bread.

notes: Baking soda in soaking water dramatically speeds cooking
Never salt until after cooking - prevents softening
Removing skins creates silkiest texture
Serve warm for authentic Israeli style

recipes.title: Maltese Pastizzi (Cheese Pies)
recipes.description: Traditional Maltese savory pastries filled with ricotta-style cheese and herbs in flaky puff pastry.

ingredients.item: fresh basil or herbs of choice

instructions.text: Preheat oven according to puff pastry package directions (usually 400°F).
Mix cheese, egg, and herbs thoroughly. Drain any excess whey.
Roll puff pastry thinner than usual.
Cut each sheet into 9 equal squares.
Place 1 tsp cheese mixture in center of each square.
Fold two opposite corners over the filling.
Twist remaining two corners like a candy wrapper.
Trim excess pastry from twisted ends.
Place on parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake until golden brown, about 15-20 minutes.

notes: Can be frozen before baking
Thaw before baking or add a few extra minutes
Traditional Maltese cheese can be substituted with ricotta
Serve with marinara or preferred dipping sauce

missing_inputs: 2 tbsp chopped fresh basil or herbs of choice

recipes.title: Feta and Pumpkin Pastries
recipes.description: Flaky filo triangles filled with roasted butternut pumpkin and tangy feta cheese.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place pumpkin cubes on baking tray. Crush garlic over top.
Drizzle with herb oil, season with salt and pepper.
Roast until pumpkin is soft, about 25-30 minutes.
Transfer roasted pumpkin to bowl. Add feta.
Mash together with potato masher. Adjust seasoning.
Layer two filo sheets together, brush with melted butter.
Cut lengthwise into 3 strips.
Place spoonful of filling at bottom of each strip.
Fold diagonally up the strip to form triangles.
Brush tops with butter.
Bake about 15-20 minutes until golden brown.

notes: Don't overfill or they may burst open
Can be frozen before baking
Serve with dipping sauce of choice
Butternut can be substituted with other squash

recipes.title: Hillbilly Fondue
recipes.description: A simple Swiss and Gruyere cheese fondue made in a double boiler. Perfect for dipping French bread.

instructions.text: Set up a double boiler (one pot nested in another containing hot water).
Rub the inside of the top pot with garlic. Discard the garlic clove(s).
Combine cornstarch with the grated cheeses.
Simmer the wine in the top pot of your double boiler. Heat should be at medium or less.
Add Swiss cheese and Gruyere cheese a bit at a time making sure the cheese is melted before adding more. Stir constantly.
Add nutmeg if desired.
Place the pot on a hotplate set to low heat to maintain the fondue's melting consistency.
Spear bread pieces on a fork and dip into the fondue.

notes: Double quantities for 4 servings
Any cheese that melts easily works well

recipes.title: Harvest Chicken Liver Pâté
recipes.description: A rich and flavorful chicken liver pâté with apple, bourbon, and warm spices. Perfect for entertaining.

ingredients.item: large tart apple, peeled, cored and chopped

instructions.text: Clean livers by removing fibrous bits and dark spots, rinse well, and soak in milk for 24 hours (optional but recommended). Drain, rinse, and pat dry.
Sauté bacon in butter until crispy. Add onion, celery, and garlic. Sauté until tender.
Add apple and livers, cooking until livers are firm but pink inside and apple softens. Add sage, allspice, and nutmeg, cooking one minute more.
Transfer to bowl. Deglaze pan with bourbon, reducing to 3 tablespoons, then transfer to bowl with seasonings and cream if desired.
Purée with stick blender until smooth.
Pack into ramekins and top with clarified butter.
Refrigerate overnight or up to 10 days.

notes: Soaking livers in milk removes bitterness
Serve with sliced baguette, crackers or mini toasts

missing_inputs: 1  large tart apple, peeled, cored and chopped

recipes.title: Deep Fried Cheese Curds
recipes.description: Classic Wisconsin-style fried cheese curds with a light, crispy batter. A state fair favorite.

instructions.text: In a medium bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Stir in the eggs and milk. Mix until smooth. Add more milk for a thinner batter.
Coat the cheese curds with the batter.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy skillet over medium heat to 375°F.
Fry the coated cheese curds approximately 1 minute each, until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

notes: Freezing curds before breading prevents cheese from liquefying
Serve immediately while hot and gooey
Fresh curds that squeak are best

recipes.title: Tyropites (Greek Cheese Pies)
recipes.source_note: CheeseForum.org - Favorite Recipes (reconstructed from traditional recipe)
recipes.description: Flaky phyllo triangles filled with a mixture of feta and ricotta cheese. A beloved Greek appetizer or snack.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a bowl, mix feta, ricotta, eggs, dill (if using), and pepper until well combined.
Unroll phyllo and cover with a damp towel to prevent drying.
Take one sheet of phyllo, brush lightly with melted butter, and fold in half lengthwise.
Brush the folded strip with more butter.
Place a heaping tablespoon of filling at one end of the strip.
Fold the corner over the filling to form a triangle, then continue folding (like folding a flag) to the end of the strip.
Brush the outside with butter and place seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Repeat with remaining phyllo and filling.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Let cool slightly before serving (filling will be very hot).

notes: Can be frozen unbaked - bake from frozen adding 5-10 minutes
Similar to spanakopita but without spinach
Some versions add a pinch of nutmeg

flags: Recipe reconstructed from forum discussion of traditional method

recipes.title: Baked Ricotta
recipes.description: A simple, elegant appetizer of creamy baked ricotta served with crusty bread.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
If ricotta is very wet, drain in cheesecloth for 30 minutes.
Mix ricotta with 1 tbsp olive oil, garlic, herbs, lemon zest, salt, and pepper.
Transfer to a small oven-safe dish. Smooth top.
Drizzle remaining olive oil over top.
Bake 40-45 minutes until golden on top.
Let rest 5 minutes. Drizzle with more olive oil.
Serve warm with sliced crusty bread.

notes: Top with cherry tomatoes before baking for variation
Best with homemade ricotta

missing_inputs: 1 tbsp chopped fresh herbs (thyme, rosemary, or oregano)

recipes.title: Lemony Baked Ricotta with Herbs
recipes.description: A delicious appetizer of warm ricotta baked with lemon zest and herbs until bubbly and slightly browned. Perfect served with toasted baguette slices.

ingredients.item: dried herbs (Italian blend or herbs de Provence)

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix lemon zest into warm ricotta.
Add 1 teaspoon dried herbs and sea salt to taste; stir to combine.
Coat an oven-proof skillet with 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Spoon ricotta mixture into the skillet.
Drizzle with additional olive oil and sprinkle remaining herbs on top.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes until bubbly and slightly browned.
Serve warm with lightly toasted baguette slices.

notes: Can use store-bought or homemade ricotta
Best served immediately while warm and bubbly
Try different herb combinations based on preference

missing_inputs: 1 1/2 teaspoons dried herbs (Italian blend or herbs de Provence)

recipes.title: Greek Layer Dip
recipes.source_note: The Art of Cheese - theartofcheese.com (June Small, The Small Farm)
recipes.description: A Mediterranean-inspired layered dip with hummus, pesto, artichokes, fresh vegetables, olives, and crumbled feta. Perfect for parties.

instructions.text: Spread hummus evenly across the bottom of a serving dish.
Layer pesto over the hummus.
Scatter chopped marinated artichokes over pesto.
Add layer of finely chopped cucumber.
Add layer of finely chopped grape tomatoes.
Scatter coarsely chopped olives on top.
Top with crumbled feta cheese.
For best flavor, chill in refrigerator for a couple of hours before serving.
Serve with pita chips.

notes: Can use homemade feta for even better flavor
Marinated feta adds extra flavor dimension
Layers can be adjusted based on preference

recipes.title: Pork Dumplings
recipes.description: Pork and chive dumplings with black vinegar dipping sauce

instructions.text: Mix flour and salt, gradually add water while stirring. Knead until smooth, rest 1 hour.
Combine pork with mushrooms, garlic, ginger, chives, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Roll dough into thin wrappers about 3.5 inches in diameter.
Fill each wrapper with 1 tbsp filling, fold and pleat edges to seal.
Pan-fry dumplings in oil, add water, cover and steam 5-7 minutes.
Remove lid, crisp bottoms 1-2 minutes. Serve with black vinegar dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Baked Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Crispy baked chicken wings with hot sauce glaze

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Pat wings dry, season with garlic powder, paprika, and salt.
Heat oil and butter in oven-safe pan. Brown wings on both sides.
Transfer to oven, bake 15 minutes until cooked to 165°F.
Toss with hot sauce and additional butter. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chilli Beef Lettuce Wraps
recipes.description: Spicy beef and pork mince in crisp lettuce cups

instructions.text: Brown mixed mince in oil until crispy. Drain excess fat.
Add garlic, ginger, and chillies with sesame oil. Cook 2 minutes.
Add sugar and fish sauce. Stir in lime zest, juice, and spring onions.
Make dressing with soy, lime, sesame oil, chilli, coriander, fish sauce, and sugar.
Spoon mince into lettuce cups, drizzle with dressing and serve.

recipes.title: Classic Swiss Cheese Fondue
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss fondue with Gruyère and Emmental, white wine, and kirsch. Perfect for sharing.

instructions.text: Rub fondue pot with cut garlic. Discard garlic.
Add wine and lemon juice. Heat over medium until simmering.
Toss cheeses with cornstarch.
Add cheese by handfuls, stirring constantly in a figure-8 motion.
Wait for each addition to melt before adding more.
Once smooth, stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper.
Transfer to fondue pot over low flame.
Serve with bread cubes for dipping. Stir occasionally.

notes: If fondue gets too thick, add a splash of warm wine
Also great with apple slices, vegetables, or small potatoes

recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs

ingredients.item: fresh pickled cucumber slices, for serving

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion, season with salt and cook until golden brown, 4 to 6 minutes; set aside.

Combine ½ cup breadcrumbs and the milk in a bowl; set aside until the milk is absorbed, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir the sherry and mustard powder in a large bowl until dissolved, then beat in 1 egg. Add the soaked breadcrumbs, the browned onion, the pork, turkey, honey, allspice, 2 teaspoons salt, and pepper to taste. Gently mix with your hands until combined.

Dampen your hands; form the mixture into 36 small meatballs, about 1 tablespoon each. Put on a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.

Put the remaining 1 cup breadcrumbs in a shallow dish. Whisk the remaining 2 eggs and 2 tablespoons water in a bowl. Dip each meatball in egg, letting the excess drip off, then roll in the breadcrumbs; return to the baking sheet.

Heat about 1½ inches vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat until a deep-fry thermometer registers 325°. Working in batches, fry the meatballs, gently stirring with a slotted spoon, until golden and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and season with salt. Let stand 10 minutes.
Fold the lingonberry preserves into the sour cream and top with the dill. Skewer each meatball with a pickled cucumber slice and serve with the lingonberry cream.

notes: After you shape and bread the meatballs, you can freeze them for up to 2 weeks. To cook, fry for 5 to 6 minutes (do not thaw).
Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Let stand 10 minutes after frying.

recipes.title: Peppered Whipped Goat Cheese
recipes.description: Light, creamy whipped goat cheese seasoned with black pepper.

instructions.text: Using a hand mixer or fork, whip the goat cheese, cream, salt and pepper until light, creamy, and fluffy.

recipes.title: Garlic Crostini
recipes.description: Simple garlic-rubbed toasted bread for serving with soups and stews.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Rub the baguette slices with the halved garlic clove on both sides and brush with olive oil.
Arrange on a small baking sheet and bake about 6 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden brown.

recipes.title: Beef Carpaccio with Pickled Radish, Fennel and Carrots, and Yuzu Vinaigrette
recipes.source_note: Gordon Ramsay's Hell's Kitchen Cookbook, pages 93-95
recipes.description: Paper-thin raw beef tenderloin served with tangy pickled vegetables and a Japanese-inspired yuzu vinaigrette. This dish appears as the first course in the Meat Lover's menu.

ingredients.prep_note: thinly sliced on mandoline, plus fronds for garnish
thinly sliced (remove seeds for less spicy)

instructions.text: FOR THE PICKLED RADISH, FENNEL, AND CARROT (make one day ahead): In a small saucepan, heat the vinegars, sugar, mustard seeds, and salt, mixing to dissolve. Bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat and cool slightly.

Combine the radishes, carrots, fennel, garlic clove, black peppercorns, and jalapeño in a bowl. Pour the vinegar mixture over the vegetables, mixing to combine. Fold in the cilantro. Transfer to a jar fitted with an airtight lid.

FOR THE YUZU VINAIGRETTE: In a small bowl, whisk together the yuzu juice, mustard, soy sauce, garlic, and lemon zest. Add the oil in a slow, steady stream, whisking to emulsify. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
FOR THE BEEF CARPACCIO: Wrap the tenderloin in plastic wrap and place in the freezer for 2 hours.

Unwrap the meat and thinly slice into 1/4-inch-thick pieces. Lay the meat onto a large sheet of plastic wrap. Top with another sheet of plastic wrap and gently pound the meat with a meat mallet until paper thin.
TO PLATE: Divide the carpaccio among four plates. Top with pickled vegetables, fennel fronds, and drizzle with yuzu vinaigrette.

notes: The pickled vegetables must be set up a day ahead.
tips: Be particularly choosy with your meat in this recipe, as carpaccio is, plain and simple, raw beef ('cooked carpaccio' is an oxymoron), pounded to tenderness to turn it into a delicacy.
Get out your sharpest chef's knife to cut your beef super-thin; freezing the tenderloin briefly beforehand makes slicing easier.
Alternatively, you might ask your butcher to slice your beef for you.

substitutions.note: use 1 tbsp grapefruit instead of 2 tbsp yuzu; yuzu is a tart Japanese citrus similar to grapefruit with notes of mandarin orange

recipes.title: Goat Cheese Croquette
recipes.description: Crispy breaded goat cheese disks with fresh herbs.

instructions.text: In a mini food processor or spice grinder, pulse the breadcrumbs until finely ground. In a medium bowl, combine the breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, and chopped chives.

Remove the goat cheese from the refrigerator. With an ice cream scoop or a tablespoon, scoop 1/4 cup of goat cheese. Place the flour in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Place the egg in another bowl and beat lightly.
Using a fork, flatten the goat cheese slightly to form a disk and toss it in the flour. Then coat the disk with beaten egg and roll in the breadcrumb mixture until evenly coated.
Repeat with remaining goat cheese. Cover loosely and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Gently add the chilled cheese croquettes. Fry until golden brown, 1/2-1 minute per side. Transfer to paper towels to drain.

tips: Keep goat cheese well chilled - it's much easier to handle.
Refrigerating the breaded croquettes for 30 minutes helps them hold together during frying.

recipes.title: Crab Shrimp Lettuce Cups with Black Bean Mango Salsa and Chili Vinaigrette
recipes.source_note: Gordon Ramsay's Hell's Kitchen Cookbook, pages 101-103
recipes.description: Light summer appetizer with marinated shrimp and crab served in butter lettuce cups with tropical salsa and spicy vinaigrette.

instructions.text: FOR THE SHRIMP: In a medium bowl, combine lime juice, oil, soy sauce, ginger, and garlic. Add shrimp and let marinate in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
WHILE the shrimp is marinating, make the salsa.

FOR THE BLACK BEAN MANGO SALSA: In a medium bowl, combine the black beans, mango, red onion, yellow pepper, jalapeño, and garlic. Add the vinegar, sugar, lime juice, and salt and pepper, and mix well. Fold in the cilantro and allow to sit at room temperature so the flavors will develop.
FOR THE CHILI VINAIGRETTE: Combine the lime juice, sherry vinegar, garlic, cayenne, cumin, and salt in a bowl. Whisk in the oil until emulsified. Stir in the parsley and set aside.

COOK THE SHRIMP AND CRAB MEAT: Heat a medium skillet, preferably nonstick, over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and cook 3 minutes total, turning once to cook both sides or until shrimp are pink. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the crabmeat. Add 3/4 teaspoon vinaigrette and season to taste. Allow to cool before plating.

TO PLATE: Separate the lettuce into leaves. Spoon about 1/4 cup black bean mango relish into the center. Top with sliced avocado, shrimp, and crab. Drizzle with tomatillo salsa and chili vinaigrette and garnish with shredded jicama and chopped chives.

notes: Only the shrimp requires cooking - just 3 minutes of stove-top time.
tips: This is a perfect light summer appetizer that requires minimal cooking.

recipes.title: Seared Foie Gras on Brioche French Toast with Caramelized Apples and Figs
recipes.description: The ultimate in opulence - incredibly rich foie gras served atop the best French toast with caramelized apples and figs. Holli Ugalde served this as starter to her Season 7 competition-winning dinner.

ingredients.item: Grade-A duck or goose foie gras
ingredients.prep_note: veins and impurities removed, cut with a heated knife into four 1/2-inch-thick slices, refrigerated until ready to use

instructions.text: FOR THE FOIE GRAS: Season the foie gras on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat a sauté pan until very hot.
Add the foie gras and sear 30-45 seconds on each side until golden.

TO PLATE: Place one slice of French toast on each plate. Top with one slice foie gras and serve with caramelized apples and figs. Drizzle the foie gras with the sauce and spoon more around the plate. Garnish with mint.

tips: Foie gras is available at specialty grocers and some butcher shops; it may require a special order.

missing_inputs: 1/2 lb Grade-A duck or goose foie gras

recipes.title: Shallot and Caramelized Onion Tarte Tatin
recipes.description: An upside-down tart made with caramelized onions and shallots. Using store-bought puff pastry makes this recipe a cinch.

instructions.text: To make onion jam for the tarte Tatin, heat a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil and garlic and stir occasionally until starting to color, 2 minutes.

Add 1 tablespoon butter and onions, and stir frequently for 6-7 minutes until the onions are translucent. Add 1 tablespoon sugar and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until onions begin to break down, about 10 minutes.

Stir in the balsamic vinegar, add thyme sprigs, and adjust heat to maintain a moderate simmer. Stir frequently until the onions are jammy, 30-35 minutes. Remove the thyme sprigs, season to taste, and set aside to cool.

Peel and trim the roots of the shallots without cutting off the core; you want the shallots to stay together. If the shallot has two lobes, separate the lobes. If you have some larger shallots, cut them in half lengthwise.
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat; add the remaining olive oil, then the shallots. Stir occasionally, being careful to keep the shallots intact. Cook until golden, 4-5 minutes.
Add the other tablespoon of sugar and cook for 3 minutes, then add the remaining butter. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the shallots are a deep caramel color, about 5 minutes.
Add red wine vinegar, season to taste, and cook until shallots are soft, about 5 more minutes. Allow to cool.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Trim the pastry into a 9-inch round. Keep refrigerated until ready for use. Cut a 9-inch circle of parchment paper and lay it in the bottom of a 9-inch cake pan.

Starting in the middle of the pan, arrange the shallots in a circular pattern, snugly together in one layer, leaving about 1/2 inch between the shallots and the edge of the pan. Then spread the onion jam over the shallots.
Lay the puff pastry on top of the shallots and onions and tuck the dough snugly around the shallots.
Bake the tart in the center of the oven for 30 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Allow to cool for 5 minutes.
Loosen the edges with a small knife and then carefully invert the tart onto a plate. Top with goat cheese.

tips: Choose a puff pastry made with butter rather than vegetable oil for the most flavorful and flaky tarte Tatin.

recipes.title: A Trio of Oysters: Tempura-Fried Oysters with Citrus Aioli, Freshly Shucked Oysters with Bloody Mary Granita, Baked Oysters Rockefeller
recipes.description: Raw, baked, and fried - this threesome of oysters is a decidedly upscale start to a meal. Blue Point oysters prepared three ways.

ingredients.item: Newcastle Brown Ale or any pale ale

ingredients.prep_note: white and green parts thinly sliced on the diagonal, for garnish

instructions.text: FOR THE FRIED OYSTERS: Pour 1 1/2-2 inches of oil in a small sauce pot and heat to 350°F.

Meanwhile, mix dry ingredients together in a mixing bowl. Add ale to dry ingredients until you reach desired consistency, mixing gently with a fork. The batter should be somewhat lumpy. Set up a bowl of ice and nestle the bowl of batter in the ice.

When the oil is to temperature, dredge oysters in the batter. Carefully add the oysters to the hot oil and cook, turning occasionally until golden on all sides, 1-2 minutes. Remove the oysters with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper-towel-lined plate. Season with salt.
TO PLATE FRESH OYSTERS: Top two fresh oysters with the Bloody Mary granita and garnish with celery salt and celery leaves.
TO PLATE BAKED OYSTERS ROCKEFELLER: Serve two oysters Rockefeller per person.
TO PLATE FRIED OYSTERS: Place each oyster in an empty oyster shell, two per plate. Serve with a dollop of aioli and garnish with scallions.

tips: To open an oyster, you'll need a short, thin-edged knife (purchase a dedicated oyster knife if you find yourself serving oysters often) that's strong enough to pry open the shells; a flat screwdriver will do in a pinch.

Hold an oyster with a kitchen towel and insert the knife between the two shells to find the hinge; pop open the oyster by twisting the knife blade, then carefully slide the knife between the shells to separate them and remove the top shell, keeping as much of the liquid from the oysters as possible.

recipes.title: Bloody Mary Granita
recipes.description: Frozen Bloody Mary mixture to top fresh oysters.

ingredients.item: olive juice from pimento stuffed green olives

instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk the V8 juice, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish, hot sauce, parsley, a few grinds of pepper, celery salt, lemon juice, and olive juice, if using.
Pour into a 8-inch metal pie plate. Freeze for at least 1 hour.

recipes.title: Oysters Rockefeller
recipes.description: Classic baked oysters with spinach, bacon, Parmesan, and a drizzle of Pernod.

instructions.text: Have a bowl of ice water ready. Bring 2 quarts of salted water to a boil. Add spinach and blanch for 3 minutes. Drain in a colander, then plunge the spinach in the ice water to stop cooking. Squeeze the spinach to get the remaining water out, then finely chop and set aside.
While the spinach is blanching, cook the bacon in a medium sauté pan until crispy. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate, then crumble and set aside.
Preheat the broiler.

In a medium sauté pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium. Add shallots and garlic and cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Add the white wine and reduce to almost dry. Stir in Parmesan and season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the chopped spinach to the pan and mix to combine.

Arrange the reserved oyster shells on the baking sheet. Put 1 oyster in each shell and top with 2-3 tablespoons of the sauce, spreading the sauce evenly out to the edge of the shell to completely cover the oyster.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs, bacon, more Parmesan, and a drizzle of Pernod. Broil for about 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Seared Foie Gras on Brioche French Toast with Caramelized Apples and Figs
recipes.description: Foie gras, made from duck or goose liver, is a French delicacy and the ultimate in opulence. The name translates to 'fat liver,' and it is incredibly rich. It's often made into pate, but here we serve it in slices set atop the best French toast you'll ever eat, with caramelized apples and figs to further gild the lily. Holli Ugalde served a version of this dish as starter to her Season 7 competition-winning dinner.

ingredients.item: Granny Smith apple, peeled and sliced into 12 slices
firm ripe black mission figs, halved lengthwise
kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
vanilla bean, seed scraped, or vanilla extract
Grade-A duck or goose foie gras, veins and impurities removed, cut into four 1/2-inch-thick slices

instructions.text: For the caramelized apples and figs: Melt the butter in a medium saute pan over medium heat. As it begins to foam, add the sugar, mixing until it dissolves. Add the apples in a single layer. Saute until brown and tender, about 8 minutes. Add the figs and cook cut side down 2-3 minutes, or until they begin to brown. Season with salt and pepper and transfer the apples and figs to a plate to keep warm.
Add the cream to the pan and mix until the sugar and butter are completely combined and a rich caramel color. Set aside and keep warm.
For the French toast: Preheat the oven to 200°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Cut the slices of bread in half.

In a shallow bowl, whisk together the eggs, vanilla, ginger, and cream. Heat the grapeseed oil in a nonstick saute pan over medium heat. Dip the brioche in the egg mixture, then add it to the pan and cook 2 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook 1 more minute. Transfer the French toast to the lined baking sheet and place in the oven to keep warm.
For the foie gras: Season the foie gras on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat a saute pan until very hot. Add the foie gras and sear 30-45 seconds on each side until golden.

To plate: Place one slice of French toast on each plate. Top with one slice foie gras and serve with caramelized apples and figs. Drizzle the foie gras with the sauce and spoon more around the plate. Garnish with mint.

recipes.title: Fig Brulee
recipes.description: Addictive whipped fig brie stuffed into halved figs and torched with a caramelized sugar top. Great for a party — stuff ahead and torch right before serving.

instructions.text: Halve the figs and carefully scoop insides into a food processor.
Remove brie rind and add cheese to processor with honey and salt. Process until smooth.
Transfer mixture to piping bag or Ziploc with corner cut off.
Stuff hollowed figs, avoiding overfilling.
Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes (up to 24 hours).
Coat stuffed figs in sugar, then torch to caramelize.

notes: Includes 30 minutes chill time.
tips: Apply sugar in a thin, even layer by rolling figs rather than sprinkling.
Keep the torch moving in circular motions to caramelize evenly without burning.

recipes.title: Blue Cheese Olive Dip (Dirty Martini Dip)
recipes.description: A creamy, savory, make-ahead party appetizer that tastes like a dirty martini in every bite. Blue cheese and briny olives with a splash of vodka.

instructions.text: Combine cream cheese, blue cheese, olive brine, vodka, chives, white pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, lemon zest, and salt in a food processor until smooth.
Refrigerate the dip while stuffing olives with blue cheese.
Transfer dip to a piping bag with large round nozzle. Pipe onto serving plate in an S pattern.
Arrange stuffed olives along the dip. Drizzle with olive oil, top with chives and black pepper. Serve with chips.

tips: This is an excellent make-ahead appetizer; prepare components ahead and assemble shortly before serving.

recipes.title: Bacon Jalapeño Popper Dip
recipes.description: Loaded jalapeño popper dip with crispy bacon, extra cheese, and the perfect amount of spice. Ultimate party appetizer.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, half the bacon, 1 cup cheddar, jalapeños, and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with remaining cheddar.
Bake 15 minutes until bubbly.
Top with remaining bacon, green onions, and cilantro.
Serve with tortilla chips.

notes: Reserve some jalapeño slices for garnish.
Use thick-cut bacon for more texture.
Can add ranch seasoning for extra flavor.

recipes.title: Bacon Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: Spicy jalapeño poppers filled with seasoned cream cheese and cheddar, wrapped in smoky bacon and baked to crispy perfection.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Mix cream cheese, cheddar, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Wrap each popper with half slice of bacon, securing with toothpick.
Arrange on baking sheet. Bake 20-25 minutes until bacon is crispy.

notes: Wear gloves when handling jalapeños.
Can be grilled instead of baked.
Remove seeds for less heat.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Dip
recipes.description: Rich, cheesy, and spicy dip made with three cheeses, tender chicken, and Buffalo sauce. Includes slow cooker and oven directions.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix cream cheese, Buffalo sauce, and ranch in a bowl until smooth.
Fold in shredded chicken and half the cheddar.
Transfer to baking dish and top with remaining cheeses.
Bake 20 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Garnish with green onions. Serve with celery, chips, or bread.

notes: For slow cooker: combine all, cook low 2-3 hours, stir occasionally.
Use rotisserie chicken for easy prep.
Adjust Buffalo sauce for desired heat level.

recipes.title: Candied Bacon Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: Jalapeños stuffed with honey-sweetened ghost pepper cream cheese, wrapped in candied bacon. Sweet and spicy perfection.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix cream cheese, 2 tbsp honey, ghost pepper flakes, and garlic powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Mix brown sugar and remaining honey. Rub over bacon slices.
Wrap each popper with candied bacon. Secure with toothpicks.
Bake 25-30 minutes until bacon is caramelized and crispy.

notes: The sweet-spicy combination is addictive.
Ghost pepper flakes add serious heat - adjust to preference.
Can smoke these for extra flavor.

recipes.title: Classic Jalapeño Poppers
recipes.description: The original crispy fried jalapeño poppers stuffed with cream cheese and coated in seasoned breading.

instructions.text: Mix cream cheese, cheddar, and garlic powder.
Fill each jalapeño half with cheese mixture.
Set up breading station: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs.
Dredge each popper in flour, dip in egg, coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F. Fry poppers 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with ranch.

notes: Can also bake at 400°F for 20 minutes.
Double-breading makes them extra crispy.
Perfect for game day or parties.

recipes.title: Crispy Buffalo Wings
recipes.description: Classic crispy buffalo wings tossed in buttery, tangy, spicy sauce. Perfect for game day or any gathering.

instructions.text: Pat wings completely dry. Toss with baking powder and salt.
Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Refrigerate 1 hour or overnight for crispier skin.
Preheat oven to 250°F. Bake wings 30 minutes.
Increase heat to 425°F. Bake 20-25 more minutes until crispy.
Make sauce: whisk melted butter, hot sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, garlic powder, and cayenne.
Toss crispy wings in buffalo sauce. Serve with blue cheese dressing and celery.

notes: Baking powder helps crisp the skin without frying.
Can also deep fry at 375°F for 10-12 minutes.

recipes.title: Ghost Pepper Wings with Buffalo-Blue Cheese Sauce
recipes.description: Crispy baked wings rubbed with ghost pepper spice, served with a creamy buffalo-blue cheese sauce. Extremely spicy!

instructions.text: Mix ghost pepper powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and baking powder.
Pat wings dry. Toss with spice mixture to coat evenly.
Place on wire rack over baking sheet. Bake at 425°F for 40-45 minutes, flipping halfway.
Make sauce: melt butter with hot sauce, then stir in blue cheese and sour cream.
Serve wings with buffalo-blue cheese sauce for dipping.

notes: Ghost pepper is extremely hot - adjust amount to preference.
Blue cheese sauce helps balance the intense heat.

recipes.title: Hot Honey Wings
recipes.description: Crispy chicken wings glazed with spicy hot honey - the perfect balance of sweet, heat, and savory.

instructions.text: Pat wings dry. Toss with baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Arrange on wire rack over baking sheet.
Bake at 425°F for 40-45 minutes until crispy, flipping halfway.
Make hot honey glaze: whisk honey, hot sauce, melted butter, cayenne, and garlic powder.
Toss crispy wings in hot honey glaze. Serve immediately while sticky and warm.

notes: The sweet-heat combo is addictive!
Add more cayenne for extra heat.

recipes.title: Jalapeño Popper Dip
recipes.description: All the flavors of jalapeño poppers in an easy, creamy, baked dip with a crunchy topping.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, cheddar, Parmesan, jalapeños, and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spread into a baking dish.
Combine panko with melted butter, sprinkle on top.
Bake 15 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Serve hot with tortilla chips, crackers, or vegetables.

notes: Add crumbled bacon for extra flavor.
Use pickled jalapeños for a tangier version.
Can be made ahead and refrigerated - add 5 minutes to baking time.

recipes.title: Queso Dip
recipes.description: Perfect gooey cheese dip with jalapeños, tomatoes, and spices. Easy to make and always a crowd pleaser.

instructions.text: Heat milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add American cheese and stir until melted.
Add cheddar cheese gradually, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomatoes with chiles, jalapeños, garlic powder, cumin, and cayenne.
Continue stirring until smooth and heated through.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

notes: Use block cheese and shred it yourself - pre-shredded has anti-clumping agents.
Keep warm in a slow cooker on low setting.
Add cooked ground beef or chorizo for a heartier version.

recipes.title: Spicy Deviled Eggs with Bacon and Jalapeño
recipes.description: Deviled eggs spiked with jalapeño, crispy bacon, and sriracha. The best deviled eggs a spicy food lover could ask for!

instructions.text: Peel hard-boiled eggs and slice in half lengthwise.
Remove yolks to a bowl and mash with a fork.
Mix yolks with mayonnaise, mustard, sriracha, jalapeño, half the bacon, and vinegar.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Pipe or spoon filling into egg white halves.
Top with remaining bacon, paprika, and chives.

notes: Perfect for holidays and game day.
Can be made ahead - store covered in fridge.
Add more sriracha for extra heat.

recipes.title: Texas Nachos
recipes.description: The ultimate appetizer with crispy corn tortillas topped with refried beans, melty cheese and pickled jalapeño peppers. Perfect for parties or game day!

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Spread tortilla chips on large baking sheet.
Warm refried beans and dollop over chips.
Top with shredded cheese and jalapeños.
Bake 10-15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Add sour cream, guacamole, and salsa. Serve immediately.

notes: Layer chips in a single layer for best results.
Add seasoned ground beef for loaded nachos.
Serve immediately - don't let them sit or chips get soggy.

recipes.title: Beef Burnt Ends
recipes.description: A barbecue appetizer featuring sticky, sweet, savory, and sumptuous bite-sized pieces of smoked brisket with bark and sauce.

instructions.text: Heat smoker to 225°F using pecan wood.
Tenderize meat with meat mallet.
Remove silver skin from meat.
Coat lightly with mayo, salt, and pepper.
Smoke until thickest part reaches 180°F.
Rest 10 minutes until safely handleable.
Cut into 1¼-inch cubes against the grain.
Toss cubes with barbecue sauce.
Add chimichurri sauce to lightly coat.
Place in disposable aluminum pan, ensuring even coating.
Return to smoker to braise for 2 hours.

notes: Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 3 months in airtight container with air removed.

recipes.title: Chicharron Burnt Ends
recipes.description: This dish combines Spanish chicharrone (pork crackling) with traditional barbecue burnt ends methodology, creating a sticky, scrumptious treat you can put out for guests.
recipes.cook_time: 3 hours (smoking) plus additional time for crisping

instructions.text: Lay out the pork belly.
Poke holes all over the fat side.
Cover with a layer of salt.
Let it sit for 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Scrape off the salt.
Finish cleaning salt with paper towel (essential to avoid oversalting).
Flip pork belly over (meat side up).
Carefully cut 2x2-inch squares without penetrating the fat layer.
Sprinkle Cuso's Hot Honey over the meat, working it into cracks.
Smoke at 225°F for 3 hours.
Transfer to a baking sheet.
Brush white vinegar over the skin.
Cook at 450°F until the skin bubbles.
Cut and serve with honey barbecue sauce drizzle.

notes: Suggested sides: avocado salad, rice and beans, salsa verde, tortillas, yuca frita.
Beverage pairings: Argentinian Malbec, ginger beer, mango juice, Negra Modelo, Sauvignon Blanc, tequila.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from appetizers category

recipes.title: Spicy Bacon Burnt Ends
recipes.description: A smoky, spiced dish with a satisfying crunch combined with a delectable interior, featuring bacon cubes with a sweet and savory glaze.

instructions.text: Preheat smoker to 275°F.
Cut bacon into 1-inch cubes.
Toss with Cuso's Maple Bourbon Seasoning, coating evenly.
Place cubes fat-side up on a rack over a baking tray.
After one hour, check internal temperature.
While smoking, combine remaining ingredients in saucepan, bring to boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
When bacon reaches 202°F, transfer to aluminum pan.
Pour sauce over cubes and toss for even coating.
Return to smoker for 30 minutes.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: The sauce creates a great texture and adds another layer of flavor.
You can prepare ahead and refrigerate overnight to let flavors develop.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from appetizers category

recipes.title: Crockpot Salsa Verde Chicken Tortilla Bowl
recipes.description: Slow-cooked chicken mixed in red salsa, salsa verde, and hot sauce, then served over rice bowls - DELISH!

ingredients.item: 2 pounds boneless chicken breasts or thighs
rice and tortilla chips, for serving
shredded lettuce, avocado, limes, and green onions, for serving

recipes.title: Spicy Chili Garlic Deviled Eggs
recipes.description: Deviled eggs with a spicy chili garlic topping featuring chili crisp, toasted sesame seeds, and soy sauce. A crowd-pleasing party appetizer.

ingredients.item: chili crisp or chili garlic oil
ingredients.prep_note: Lao Gan Ma is a great choice

instructions.text: Place eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with 1 inch of cold water. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
Once boiling, turn off the heat, cover, and let eggs sit for 10–12 minutes. Transfer to an ice bath and cool completely.
Peel the cooled eggs and slice in half lengthwise. Scoop yolks into a mixing bowl and arrange egg white halves on a serving platter.
Mash yolks with a fork until crumbly. Add mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth and creamy. Adjust seasoning to taste.
In a small bowl, mix chili crisp, toasted sesame seeds, soy sauce, garlic (if using), and sugar (if using). Stir well.

recipes.title: [323] Milk-Fed Snails
recipes.source_note: Apicius: Cookery and Dining in Imperial Rome (Project Gutenberg #29728, public domain)
recipes.description: Latin: COCHLEAS LACTE PASTAS. From Book VII - Sumptuous Dishes, Recipe #323.

instructions.text: TAKE SNAILS AND SPONGE THEM; PULL THEM OUT OF THE SHELLS BY THE MEMBRANE AND PLACE THEM FOR A DAY IN A VESSEL WITH MILK AND SALT RENEW THE MILK DAILY.

notes: Just enough so they do not drown.

The Romans raised snails for the table in special places called cochlearia. Fluvius Hirpinus is credited with having popularized the snail in Rome a little before the civil wars between Cæsar and Pompey. If we could believe Varro, snails grew to enormous proportions. Snails as a food are not sufficiently appreciated by the Germanic races who do not hesitate to eat similar animals and are very fond of such food as oysters, clams, mussels, cocles, etc., much of which they even eat in the raw state.

recipes.title: Cocktail Party Bean Dip

recipes.source_note: Hell's Kitchen cookbook (Minneapolis). Recipe from Adele, who was married to a guy named Tip who'd played football for the Chicago Bears in the thirties and forties with Bronko Nagurski.
recipes.description: A rich, cheesy bean dip with jalapeños, perfect for parties.

instructions.text: Sort through dried beans, removing any debris such as small stones. Place in large bowl and cover with water. Soak 4 hours, drain and rinse.
Place soaked beans, salt, oil, mustard, and onion chunks in a large, heavy pot, and pour in 6 cups water, making sure beans are well covered.
Heat to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer, checking occasionally, until beans are very soft, about 4 hours. If at any point evaporation exposes top layer of beans, add hot water to cover.
Drain and return to the pot.
Mash beans with a potato masher.
Stir together bean mixture, butter, provolone cheese, canned jalapeños, jalapeño liquid, minced onion, and mashed garlic.
Cook bean mixture over medium heat until cheese is absorbed, about 7 minutes.
Serve hot with corn chips or saltine crackers.
